attention.basculer.aide: Synfus brings the character to the front by itself. Handy in combat, disorienting if you are typing somewhere else.
attention.releve.sansBandeau: strip unreadable — measuring on the screen ordinate
attention.signaler.aide: The character blinks in the bar. You see where to go without being moved by force.
barre.accessibiliteRequise: Synfus needs Accessibility access to list and activate windows
barre.autreBureau: On another desktop — click to switch to it
barre.chasseAide: Treasure hunt: the map of the next clue — shortcut: %@.
barre.passageAuto.actif: Auto-switch on — Synfus switches to the character whose icon bounces (%@)
barre.passageAuto.inactif: Auto-switch off — the character is only flagged (%@)
barre.rangerAide: Arrange windows — layouts, full screen, start the session
barre.sousTitre: The character bar above the game.
barre.zaap.aucunFavori: No favourite zaap — star them in Settings › Zaap
calibration.aide: Pick an area, then draw a rectangle on the capture. Areas are fractions of the window: they follow its size, fullscreen or windowed.
carte.maj.suspecte: DofusDB only returned %lld places, the current map is kept.
chasse.aide: A floating panel: the start (your read position), a direction (buttons or arrow keys) and the clue (typed, or read on screen) give the next map from DofusDB, and its /travel is copied — through a zaap if it saves enough maps. Synfus validates nothing and sends nothing to the game: paste, walk and validate yourself. The panel takes the keyboard without leaving the game; a click in the game gives it back.
chasse.autoriser.aide: Reading clues on screen requires the “Screen Recording” permission.
chasse.indices.aucune: Clues are loaded when the panel first opens
chasse.lire.aide: Reads the hunt tracker on screen and offers the recognised clues; the last one is selected. The read area is calibrated in Diagnostics › Calibrate areas.
chasse.phorreur.suivre: Follow the direction (%@) until the Phorreur
chasse.sousTitre: The treasure hunt panel, and its clues.
classes.icones.aide:
Each class can get the image of your choice: a portrait, a screenshot, any PNG or JPEG — with “Choose…”, by drag and drop, or by dropping iop.png, cra.png… into the folder then “Reload”. Without an image, Synfus shows the colored chip.

The official emblems come from Tools/fetch-ankama-assets.sh, which downloads them for your personal use into Resources/Ankama, bundled by build.sh. Synfus redistributes no image from the game. An icon dropped here takes priority over the bundled one.
classes.mentionAnkama: Some illustrations are the property of Ankama Studio and Dofus — All rights reserved.
classes.sousTitre: One icon per class, on the bar's chips. Synfus ships none: drop your own.
combat.pasEncore: not read yet — switch to this character
diagnostic.accessibiliteManquanteQuarant: Accessibility permission missing — and this copy is quarantined, which will keep it from taking effect. See the General tab.
diagnostic.apercu.introuvable: preview: window not found at capture
diagnostic.attention.aide: Watches the only two signals an app sends outward: its window title and its Dock icon. Start the probe, play a fight, and see whether something moves when your turn comes. The icon → character pairing assumes the icons follow launch order: check that the right character is flagged. A bounce moves an icon away from its strip; at rest, the offsets must not move.
diagnostic.attention.appariementDouteux: One icon per Dofus process was expected: the pairing is unreliable here.
diagnostic.aucuneFenetre: No Dofus window detected. Is the game running?
diagnostic.fenetres.aide: The raw titles of the Dofus windows. If the name shown does not match your character, the client does not expose the name in its title; numbering then follows launch order, to be reordered in the Characters tab.
diagnostic.gelesAcheves.ligne: %@ (pid %lld) — no window and silent on three probes, force quit
diagnostic.lecture.aide: Reads, in the frontmost character's window, the position (area name and coordinates) and the combat state (coloured “End turn” button: their turn; grey: someone else's; absent: out of combat). One small area per reading, scaled to a fixed size; OCR only runs again when the area changed. “Calibrate areas” if the game interface was moved. Requires Screen Recording.
diagnostic.position.etat.attente: Waiting: no Dofus client in front. Use “Read all”, or go back to the game.
diagnostic.position.etat.preparation: Preparing OCR (first model load, up to a few tens of seconds)…
diagnostic.position.etat.sansCoordonnees: Text read, but no coordinates: look at the area below — are the coordinates in it?
diagnostic.position.illisible: no coordinates in the text read
diagnostic.position.pasEncore: position: not read yet — switch to this character
diagnostic.position.stats: %lld OCR reads (last: %lld ms) · %lld unchanged readings skipped
diagnostic.position.toutLire.aide: Reads the position of every connected character, once. The regular pass only reads the frontmost character: while the settings are open, Synfus is in front.
diagnostic.rangement.aide: A full-screen window is never moved, and a character on another desktop is out of Accessibility's reach — switch to it, then arrange again.
diagnostic.sousTitre: What Synfus sees, and the assumptions it makes.
enchainer.sousTitre: A click in the game, key held: Synfus moves to the next character.
equipes.glisserPourCreer: Drop a character here to create a team
fermeture.confirmation.detail: Each client is asked to quit, then forced if it stops responding. Characters in combat will lose their turn.
general.accessibilite.aide: Essential: this is what lets Synfus list Dofus windows, read the character's name and activate a client. Without it, no character shows up. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
general.apercus.aide: A thumbnail of the character's window when hovering its chip. A character on another desktop or in full screen elsewhere can be captured, but its image may be stale: macOS does not redraw a window it is not showing.
general.barre.aide: Move the bar by grabbing the dots on its left. It never takes the keyboard: it is a game overlay.
general.barre.position: Position at the top of the screen
general.barre.seulementDofus: Only when Dofus is in front
general.enregistrementEcran.aide: Used for window previews and screen reading (position, combat). A permission distinct from Accessibility; macOS often asks to relaunch Synfus after granting it. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording.
general.langue.aide: By default, Synfus speaks the language of macOS. The choice takes effect on the next launch — the button relaunches Synfus.
general.quarantaine: This copy is quarantined: the Accessibility permission will have no effect
general.quarantaine.aide: It was downloaded, and macOS marks it as unverified. As long as that mark is there, checking Synfus in System Settings has no effect. Run the first command in Terminal then relaunch Synfus; the second resets the entry if Synfus had already been allowed before.
general.sousTitre: Permissions, the floating bar and the system.
invitations.sousTitre: The team's /invite, copied with a shortcut.
lecture.sousTitre: Position and combat, read in the game window.
lieux.affiner: %lld results: refine the search to see more.
lieux.sousTitre: Banks, marketplaces, workshops, temples, dungeons, transport: label them, make them favorites, reach them in one click.
menu.aucunPersoEquipe: No character from this team connected
palette.cmd.invite: The whole team on one line, or one character
palette.cmd.pnj: An NPC located by quests, nearest first
palette.cmd.quete: A quest: the resources to gather and its objectives, with their route
palette.cmd.travel: A place (bank, market, smithmagic…), through the nearest zaap
palette.cmd.zaap: The zaap by name, area or your label
palette.invite: Zaap, place, quest, NPC… / commands, % variables
palette.reglages.lieux.aide: A bank, a workshop, a dungeon… is labelled (⌘E) or made a favorite (⌘D) from the palette, or with a right-click on the result.
palette.reglages.quetes.aide: Quests, their objectives and resources, and the position of the NPCs they mention: downloaded from api.dofusdb.fr the first time the palette opens, then every 30 days.
palette.reglages.sousTitre: The palette (⌘:): zaaps, places, quests, NPCs, commands — type, Return copies.
palette.reglages.tri.sousTexte: After the zaaps, always first. ⌘T changes it in the palette.
persos.acheverGeles.aide: A client that freezes while closing stays alive without any window. Synfus probes it and, silent three times in a row (~15 s), force quits it — whether the close came from Synfus or from the game. Kills are logged in Diagnostics.
persos.equipes.aide: Up to four teams, composed here or by dragging a chip onto the row that appears under the bar — onto “+” to create one, onto “All” to leave. The active team restricts the bar, ⌘1…⌘n, next/previous, arranging and the overview; the other characters stay under “All”. Synfus always starts on “All”.
persos.ordre.aide: The order decides slot numbering. Characters not connected are skipped: keep as many as you like. Drag a row, or use the arrows.
persos.sousTitre: Character order sets their number; teams narrow the bar.
pnj.sousTitre: NPCs located by quests. DofusDB doesn't say whether they're just passing by: the most cited spot comes first.
quete.aucune: No pinned quest: Return on a quest in the palette, or Settings → Quests.
quete.copierNom: Copy the name, for the market
quetes.maj.suspecte: DofusDB only returned %lld quests, the current ones are kept.
quetes.sousTitre: A quest opens in a transparent panel above the game: resources and routes in one click.
raccourci.enregistrer.aide: Click, then press the combination. A global shortcut needs at least one modifier.
raccourci.pressez.aide: Press the combination, or Esc to cancel.
raccourcis.allerAUnPerso.aide: Slots follow the order of the Characters tab; characters not connected are skipped, numbers stay stable.
raccourcis.attention: When a character calls for attention
raccourcis.attention.aide: Detected from the icon bouncing in the Dock, the only signal an app can send outward; Synfus reads nothing from the game itself.
raccourcis.attention.bascule: Turn automatic switching on or off
raccourcis.conflit: This combination is already assigned to another action: the system keeps only one.
raccourcis.enchainer.aide: Hold the key, click in the game: the click goes through normally, then Synfus switches to the next character — like “Next character” on the keyboard. A click without the key stays a click. You still click once per character; only the window switch is automatic. Synfus sends and replays no click.
raccourcis.enchainer.bascule: Switch to the next character after a click with the key held
raccourcis.enchainer.clicsCaptes.aide: If it stays at zero after clicking in the game, macOS is not delivering the events: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring.
raccourcis.enchainer.touche.aide: The game receives the click with the key on it, Synfus does not strip it. fn is the only one the game ignores; ⇧ and ⌥ mean something in Dofus, ⌃-click is a right click for macOS, and a ⌘-click no longer talks to NPCs. If releasing fn opens the emoji picker, set “Press 🌐 key to” to “Do Nothing” in System Settings → Keyboard.
raccourcis.equipeSuivante.aide: Cycles: all characters, team 1, team 2… then all. Teams are composed in the Characters tab or by dragging a chip onto the second row of the bar.
raccourcis.invitation.aide: Puts “/invite Name” on the clipboard, one character per press, cycling over the active team. The leader is the character in front at the first press, and stays so until the end of the round — even if auto-switch changes windows meanwhile. Paste it in the chat (⌘V ↩): Synfus sends nothing to the game.
raccourcis.invitation.format.aide: %nom is replaced by the character's name, as the game shows it in the window title. Right-clicking a chip copies that character's invitation.
raccourcis.invitation.toutes.aide: Puts "/invite A; /invite B; …" in the clipboard: the whole active team except the character in front, on one line. The game chains the commands: a single paste in the chat (⌘V ↩). Synfus sends nothing to the game.
raccourcis.inviter.aide: Synfus sends no event: it composes the command, you paste it. One gesture per guest, like one click per character.
raccourcis.lancerSession.aide: The morning gesture: arranges with the last layout, then switches to character 1.
raccourcis.palette.aide: Zaaps, places (bank, market, smithmagic…), game commands, variables, characters: type, Return copies, ⌘V pastes in the chat. / for commands, % for variables, Tab to filter, ⌘T to sort, ⌘E to label, ⌘D for a favorite.
raccourcis.ranger.aide: Replays the last layout used — side by side, grid, one large + thumbnails, stacked — chosen from the bar button, the menu bar or the right click. No default: your call.
raccourcis.refusees: Refused by the system (already taken by another app): %@
raccourcis.signalerBascule: Blink the character on each switch
raccourcis.signalerBascule.aide: Whenever Synfus switches character — shortcut, click chaining, auto-switch — its chip blinks in the bar for a second and a half.
raccourcis.sousTitre: Global shortcuts: they work even when Dofus is in front.
raccourcis.voirTous.aide: Previews stay visible as long as the combination is held. It must include a modifier, and requires the screen recording permission.
rangement.raison.autreBureau: on another desktop — switch to it then arrange again
rangement.raison.sansEcran: no screen to place it on
trajets.sousTitre: A copied /travel goes through the nearest zaap when it saves the trip.
zaap.ajout.aide: For a zaap the list doesn't know yet: it counts as a World of Twelve zaap. A zaap already listed is checked in the list.
zaap.auto.aide: Synfus looks at every new copy, from any app, and only touches a "/travel x,y" text. Passwords marked as secret are never read. macOS may ask once whether Synfus can read the clipboard.
zaap.gain.sousTexte: Below that, the /travel is left as is.
zaap.liste.aide: Uncheck a zaap so it is never suggested. Those marked "other map" (Incarnam, Canopy, Harebourg, Crocuzko) have coordinates that overlap the World of Twelve: unchecked by default, otherwise a /travel to Amakna could go through Incarnam.
zaap.maj.aide: Downloads the zaap list from api.dofusdb.fr — Synfus also does it by itself at launch when the list is more than 30 days old. Your choices, additions and favourites are kept.
zaap.raccourci.aide: Rewrites the clipboard's /travel as "/zaap x,y ; /travel a,b" when the zaap saves enough maps. Beeps when nothing changes. Paste it in the chat (⌘V ↩): Synfus sends nothing to the game.
zaap.reecriture.aide: When the copied /travel targets a map far from you but close to a zaap, Synfus prefixes it with "/zaap x,y ;" in the clipboard. Only a "/travel x,y" text is looked at: anything else is left untouched. Your position is the one OCR reads on the last character in front.
zaaps.sousTitre: %lld active out of %lld — the palette and /travel rewriting only offer active ones.
